1. Number Series    ----- Done 
A sequence of numbers is given with one number missing. You must identify the pattern and fill in the blank.

Example: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___
Answer: 42 (differences: 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2. Alphabet Series / Coding-Decoding
Letters are rearranged or coded according to a rule. You must decode or continue the pattern.

Example: If CAT = XZG, then DOG = ?
Answer: WLT (each letter replaced by its mirror in the alphabet)

3. Analogies (Word Pairs)
Identifying the relationship between a given pair of words and applying it to a second pair.

Example: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ___
Answer: School

4. Odd One Out
Four or five options are given; three share a common property and one does not.

Example: Mango, Apple, Banana, Carrot
Answer: Carrot (it’s a vegetable, not a fruit)

5. Synonyms & Antonyms
A word is given and you must select the closest meaning (synonym) or opposite meaning (antonym) from four options.

6. Sentence Completion / Jumbled Words
A sentence with a blank is given, or words are jumbled and you must form a meaningful sentence. Tests command of English and logical sentence structure.

7. Arithmetic Problems
Simple arithmetic — percentages, ratios, time-distance, profit-loss — at Class 8–9 difficulty level. Speed matters more than complexity here.

8. Common Sense / Logical Reasoning
Short logical puzzles — blood relations, seating arrangements, direction sense — testing your ability to reason quickly from given conditions.

SSB OIR Test: Non-Verbal Reasoning (Booklet 2)
The non-verbal booklet replaces words with shapes, patterns, and figures. It is considered more challenging by most candidates because it cannot be prepared through rote learning — only practice builds speed.

1. Figure Series Completion
A series of figures is shown with a blank. You must identify the pattern (rotation, reflection, number of elements) and pick the figure that correctly fills the blank.

2. Odd Figure Out
Five figures are shown; four share a common property (size, shading, orientation). You must identify the one that doesn’t fit.

3. Analogy (Figure Pairs)
A pair of figures is shown with a specific relationship (e.g., one is rotated 90° clockwise from the other). A third figure is given — you must select the fourth figure that has the same relationship.

4. Mirror Images
A figure is shown. You must pick which of the four options is its correct mirror image (flipped horizontally).

5. Embedded / Hidden Figures
A simple shape (e.g., a triangle) is shown, and four complex figures are given. You must identify in which complex figure the simple shape is hidden or embedded.

6. Paper Folding & Cutting
A paper is shown being folded and then punched/cut. You must identify what the paper looks like when unfolded.

7. Counting Figures
A complex figure made up of triangles, squares, or rectangles is shown. You must count the total number of a specific shape within it.

Part 1: Verbal Reasoning

• 1. Number and Letter Series Completion
	• Concept: Identifying the logical pattern in a sequence of numbers or letters to find the next item.
	• Example: Complete the series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
	• Answer: 127 (Pattern: Multiply by 2 and add 1 → 63 × 2 + 1 = 127).
• 2. Coding and Decoding
	• Concept: Words are encrypted based on a specific rule, and you must apply that rule to decode a new word.
	• Example: If BOMBAY is coded as CPNCBZ, how will DELHI be coded?
	• Answer: EFMIJ (Pattern: Each letter shifts forward by one position).
• 3. Odd One Out / Classification
	• Concept: Picking the word or number that does not belong to the group.
	• Example: Choose the odd one out: (a) Chennai, (b) Mumbai, (c) Bengaluru, (d) Punjab.
	• Answer: (d) Punjab (It is a state, while the rest are state capitals).
• 4. Analogies
	• Concept: Finding a relationship between two words or numbers and applying it to another pair.
	• Example: Architect : Building :: Sculptor : ____
	• Answer: Statue (An architect designs a building; a sculptor shapes a statue).
• 5. Blood Relations
	• Concept: Deciphering complex family trees based on a given statement.
	• Example: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, "I have no brother or sister but that man’s father is my father’s son." Whose photograph was it?
	• Answer: His son's photograph ("My father's son" is the man himself since he has no siblings. So, the man in the photo's father is him).
• 6. Direction Sense Test
	• Concept: Tracking movements in directions (North, South, East, West) to find final placement or distance.
	• Example: A person walks 4 km North, then turns right and walks 3 km. How far is he from his starting point?
	• Answer: 5 km (Using Pythagoras theorem: \(\sqrt{4^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5\)).
• 7. Word Rearrangement and Dictionary Order
	• Concept: Unscrambling letters to make meaningful words, or arranging words alphabetically.
	• Example: Unscramble TEACRHE to form a meaningful word.
	• Answer: TEACHER.
• 8. Jumbled Sentences & Logical Order
	• Concept: Arranging statements in a sequential timeline.
	• Example: Arrange in logical order: 1. Core, 2. Harvest, 3. Seed, 4. Plant.
	• Answer: 3, 4, 2, 1 (Seed → Plant → Harvest → Core/Fruit).

Part 2: Non-Verbal Reasoning

These questions rely completely on diagrams, shapes, and figures to judge your spatial intelligence.
• 1. Figure Series Completion
	• Concept: Identifying how a geometric shape changes across a sequence (e.g., rotating clockwise) to guess the next frame.
	• Example: A line inside a square rotates 45 degrees clockwise in each step.
	• Format: You will select the next correct diagram from 4 options showing the next 45-degree rotation.
• 2. Figure Analogy
	• Concept: Figuring out how Figure A transforms into Figure B, and applying that exact rule to transform Figure C into Figure D.
	• Example: If a triangle turns upside down and changes its colour to black, you must do the exact same to a circle or square presented as the third figure.
• 3. Spotting the Embedded Figure
	• Concept: Finding a small, hidden geometrical shape inside a larger, complex diagram.
	• Format: A simple "Z" or "X" shape is given, and you must choose which complex drawing completely hides that specific shape within its lines.
• 4. Paper Cutting and Folding
	• Concept: Visualising how a piece of paper will look after it is folded, punched with holes/cuts, and unfolded again.
	• Format: You are shown a square paper folded twice into a smaller square with a circular punch in the corner. You must identify the correct unfolded pattern showing 4 holes.
• 5. Cube and Dice Problems
	• Concept: Identifying opposite faces of a folded box or a rolled dice.
	• Example: You are shown three different angles of the same dice with numbers 1 to 6. You are asked: "Which number is opposite to 4?"
	• Answer: You solve this by finding common adjacent numbers across the views to rule out incorrect options.
• 6. Mirror and Water Images
	• Concept: Visualising the exact lateral inversion (Mirror) or vertical inversion (Water) of an object or word.
	• Example: Find the mirror image of the word SSB when the mirror is placed on the right.
	• Answer: 𐐒ƧƧ (Letters reverse position and flip horizontally).
• 7. Matrix/Figure Completion
	• Concept: A large pattern (often a 3 × 3 grid) has one missing piece. You must find the missing fragment to complete the design symmetry.

A. Required academic and application documents

Carry the original plus 2 photocopies, self-attested, for the certificates listed below where the call-up letter specifies this. Keep originals separate from the photocopies.
[ ] Online application form — 2 copies. Print both, sign them, self-attest, and attach a photograph to each copy.

[ ] 10th / Matriculation certificate and passing certificate — original + 2 self-attested photocopies. This is required as proof of your name, parents’ names and date of birth. The letter says a marksheet, admit card, TC or school-leaving certificate is not accepted instead of the required certificate.

[ ] 12th certificate and marksheet — original + 2 self-attested photocopies. If you entered through a diploma route, carry the diploma certificate and marksheets as applicable.

[ ] B.Tech degree certificate or provisional degree certificate — original + 2 self-attested photocopies.

[ ] B.Tech marksheets — original marksheets for every semester + 2 self-attested photocopies of each. Keep them in semester order.

[ ] Cumulative percentage certificate — original + 2 self-attested photocopies. It should show the cumulative percentage through the final semester/year and be issued/certified by the Controller of Examinations, Registrar, Dean or Principal as specified by the letter.

[ ] CGPA conversion proof — original + 2 copies if issued as a separate certificate. Since your CMM shows percentage calculation, carry the CMM too. Make sure the official conversion formula is clear.


B. Your CGPA / branch declarations
[ ] Appendix A — CGPA undertaking for passed engineering graduates. Fill your name, roll number, course, branch, final CGPA, maximum CGPA, official conversion formula and converted percentage. The format includes a university/college countersignature and stamp section.

[ ] Appendix E — Branch of Engineering declaration. Fill your branch as it appears on your degree/marksheets and the cumulative percentage requested by the form. Sign and date it.

[ ] Appendix H — Risk certificate. Type or handwrite it on plain paper and have your parent/guardian sign it, following the supplied specimen.

[ ] Appendix O — No duplicate profile/registration ID declaration. Complete and sign as specified.

[ ] Appendix P — Eligibility undertaking. Complete and sign.

[ ] Appendix Q — Previous debarment / academy withdrawal declaration. Complete truthfully and sign.


C. Conditional documents — carry only if they apply
[ ] Appendix F: Bonafide certificate and certified true copies if your original certificates/marksheets are deposited with your college/institution for higher studies.

[ ] Appendix G: Original affidavit if your name or a parent’s name differs between your online application and certificates.

[ ] Appendices J/K/L: Relevant tattoo self-certification/certificate if you have a tattoo covered by the call-up letter’s tattoo instructions.

[ ] Appendix M + travel proof: If claiming TA, carry the completed TA form, original ticket/printout and other required travel/bank proof.

[ ] Appendix N: If your address changed after submitting the application.

[ ] Foreign residence documents: If you lived abroad during the last five years, carry passport/visa copies and the complete foreign address.

[ ] Court case documents: If any case is pending against you, carry the FIR and the case/police station/court details listed in the letter.

[ ] Employer clearance: If you are or were employed by a Central/State Government undertaking or autonomous body, carry the clearance certificate from the previous employer. The letter does not specifically impose this requirement merely for private employment.


D. Photographs and personal items
[ ] 30 recent passport-size photographs as specified in the letter; not older than one week at reporting. Follow the specified size/background/dress requirements in the call-up letter.

[ ] Writing material: Blue/black pens, pencil, eraser and 10 A4 sheets.

[ ] Clothing: Formal light-coloured shirt, dark trousers and formal shoes; white sports shirt, shorts and sports shoes.

[ ] Personal items: Toiletries, lock and key, water bottle, umbrella/rain protection, 2 bedsheets, 2 pillow covers and a light blanket.
